title: Uniform law of the special coordinate
statement:
Fix a positive integer $n$ and an index $i \in \{0, 1, \dots, n-1\}$. Equip the finite sample space of hard samples with its uniform probability measure. Then the probability of the event that the special coordinate $T$ equals $i$ is
\[
\frac{1}{n}.
\]
hypotheses_covered: n is a positive natural number
i is an index in Fin n
measure is the uniform (volume) probability measure on the finite hard-sample space
replaced: Under the hard distribution, the special coordinate is uniform.
